wren (family of brown passerine birds, found chiefly in the New World)
rætìn.etymology: From re (“king”) + -ìn (diminutive suffix), or borrowed from the equivalent in another Romance language. Compare Italian reattino, Venetan reatin, reatìn (“wren”).

glosses_en: emperor (type of monarch, who rules over an empire)
imperatô.etymology: In this form, borrowed from Italian imperatore.

pàize.etymology: From Late Latin pāgēnsis (“inhabitant of a district”). Compare Italian paese.

glosses_en: queen (female monarch who rules over a kingdom)

comifò.etymology: Ultimately from French comme il faut (literally “as must be”). Compare Neapolitan commifò.

mandillo.etymology: From Latin mantelium, from Ancient Greek μανδήλιον (mandḗlion, “cloth, handkerchief”).
